newsitem.title: USA: Barge traffic up on Midwest rivers, weather warms.
newsitem.headline: Barge traffic up on Midwest rivers, weather warms.

text.p: Moderating temperatures in the U.S. Midwest were helping to break up ice and ease barge travel on the Illinois and Mississippi rivers Tuesday, grain dealers and river officials said.
"We're definitely seeing more traffic," one river dealer said. "If they (barge operators) break through St. Louis and make their way to the Illinois, they should be okay."
Floating ice, loosened by above-freezing temperatures, was still causing problems for barges on the stretch of the Mississippi between St. Louis, Mo. and Cairo, Ill., cash and river officials said.
"Traffic is still slow, but the ice is breaking up" said an Army Corps on Engineers official at Lock and Dam 27, located north of St. Louis.

High temperatures on Tuesday were seen climbing to 42 to 48 degrees Fahrenheit in Illinois, while parts of Missouri were forecast to have readings in the 50s F, according to data from Weather Express forecasters in Omaha, Neb.

Some rain is also forecast for Tuesday. The precipitation would be welcomed because it would speed up the melting process. But some warned the melting ice could cause problems as it moves down river as it could create blockages.
